name: Hindalco Industries Ltd
about: Incorporated in 1958, Hindalco Industries Ltd. is a flagship company of the Aditya Birla Group. The Co and its subsidiaries are primarily engaged in the production of Aluminium and Copper. It is also engaged in the manufacturing of aluminium sheet, extrusion and light gauge products for use in packaging markets like beverage and food, can and foil products, etc. [1]

sections.one_liner: Integrated aluminium/copper major plus Novelis. Q1 FY27 EBITDA hit a record, but leverage is near the 2x cap during peak capex.
business: Integrated aluminium chain from bauxite, alumina, coal and power through smelting to downstream products; 48 units in 10 countries. [AR FY26]
Four segments: India Aluminium, Specialty Alumina (global top-3), Copper and Novelis flat-rolled products. Segment revenue shares are not disclosed. [AR FY26]
India upstream earned ₹7,390 cr EBITDA in Q1 FY27. That is about 53% of the ₹13,932 cr consolidated EBITDA, so LME exposure dominates. [Q1FY27 call][Numbers]
Novelis is the world's largest FRP producer and recycler. Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA was $516M, or $563/t, against a $600/t long-term target. [AR FY26][Q1FY27 call]
financial_snapshot: Q1 FY27: revenue ₹84,825 cr (+32% YoY), EBITDA ₹13,932 cr, PAT ₹7,013 cr (+75%). OPM of 16% is the highest in eight quarters. [Numbers]
TTM: revenue ₹2,95,537 cr, EBITDA ₹40,903 cr (13.8% margin), PAT ₹16,400 cr. [Numbers]
Stated P/E is 9.52, but TTM PAT implies about 12.1x; the inputs are not disclosed. P/B is 1.45x and yield 0.56%. [Numbers]
ROCE 13.2%, ROE 13.0%. Market cap plus FY26 gross debt is about ₹2,97,842 cr, roughly 7.3x TTM EBITDA; cash is not disclosed. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue CAGR is 15.8% over 5 years but only 7.2% over 3. FY26 grew 15.3% to ₹2,74,944 cr, and Q1 FY27 grew 32%. [Numbers]
The 30.9% 5-year PAT CAGR starts from a low FY21 base. The 3-year PAT CAGR is 9.9%, and FY26 PAT fell 16% to ₹13,391 cr. [Numbers]
FY26 EBITDA rose 9.7% while PAT fell 16%. Q3 and Q4 PAT dropped 45% and 51% YoY, the same period as the Oswego fires. [Numbers][AR FY26]
OPM is 13% versus an 11.3% prior-3-year average, yet ROCE fell from 15% to 13% because the capital base grew faster than profits. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings rose 51% in FY26 to ₹99,165 cr. D/E went from 0.53 to 0.73, the highest in four years. [Numbers]
Net debt/EBITDA went from 1.23x (Q2 FY26) to 1.73x (Q3) to 1.95x (Jun 2026). That leaves 0.05x headroom under the 2x ceiling. [Q2FY26 call][Q3FY26 call][Q1FY27 call]
Cash cycle lengthened from 51 to 65 days. Inventory days rose from 121 to 156, an estimated ₹23,000 cr tied up. Debtor days went from 30 to 36. [Numbers]
cash_quality: The 3-year CFO/PAT ratio is 1.48x. But FY26 CFO of ₹10,250 cr covered only 0.77x PAT and fell 58% YoY. [Numbers]
FCF fell from ₹9,571 cr to ₹8,378 cr to ₹4,006 cr, then −₹19,508 cr in FY26. Implied FY26 capex is about ₹29,758 cr, roughly 3x FY23. [Numbers]
FY26 profits did not turn into cash. The Oswego fires cost about $1.7B in cash and inventory built up. Insurance recovery timing is not disclosed. [AR FY26][Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: The Q4 call claimed ₹21,858 cr of cash flow (+11%). Reported FY26 CFO was ₹10,250 cr, down 58%, and the two were not reconciled. [Q4FY26 call][Numbers]
The Q3 call led with adjusted PAT up 8%, but reported Q3 PAT fell 45% to ₹2,049 cr. The adjustments were not itemised. [Q3FY26 call][Numbers]
The Q1 FY27 record matches the numbers: PAT of ₹7,013 cr is identical. EBITDA is ₹13,932 cr in the data versus ₹13,481 cr on the call. [Numbers][Q1FY27 call]
Management talks of leverage discipline, but net debt/EBITDA went from 1.23x to 1.95x in nine months. In Nov 2025 they said it 'will not cross 2' for four years. [Q2FY26 call][Q1FY27 call]
guidance: FY27 capex: ₹12,000 cr for India, above the ₹10,000–12,000 cr range given in Feb. Novelis 2.3–2.4 billion, mostly Bay Minette (currency stated as INR). [Q4FY26 call]
Consolidated net debt to peak at ₹80,000–90,000 cr within two years. Consolidated leverage to stay around 2x. [Q4FY26 call][Q3FY26 call]
Novelis: $600/t long-term EBITDA unchanged. Structural cost cut of $350–400M by FY28 exit, with $225M achieved so far. [Q1FY27 call]
Aditya smelter: first 180 pots in Dec 2027, next 180 in Dec 2028. Captive coal of about 1.5Mt arrives only in FY28. [Q4FY26 call][Q1FY27 call]
Expect normalisation: downstream about $250/t for the rest of FY27 (vs $303 in Q1); copper ₹600–700 cr per quarter (vs ₹918 cr). [Q1FY27 call][Q4FY26 call]

bull: Q1 FY27 PAT of ₹7,013 cr annualises to about ₹28,000 cr, about 7x the ₹1,98,677 cr market cap. P/B is 1.45x with 13% ROE. [Numbers]
India upstream earned a record $2,331/t. Captive coal (1.5Mt, FY28) and the Aditya smelter (Dec 2027) add low-cost integrated volume. [Q1FY27 call]
Novelis made $563/t, up 30% YoY, despite a $70M tariff hit. Cost savings are $225M of the $350–400M target. [Q1FY27 call]
bear: Q1 looks like a peak. Management guides downstream from $303 to $250/t and copper from ₹918 cr to ₹600–700 cr. [Q1FY27 call][Q4FY26 call]
FY26 FCF was −₹19,508 cr and FY27 India capex is ₹12,000 cr plus Bay Minette. Leverage is only 0.05x below the 2x cap. [Numbers][Q4FY26 call]
Oswego, Bay Minette and renewables all slipped. Bay Minette cost went from $4B to $5B, with $100–150M a year in ramp costs. [Q2FY26 call][Q4FY26 call]
questions: How does the ₹21,858 cr cash flow reconcile with FY26 reported CFO of ₹10,250 cr?
What below-EBITDA items cut Q3–Q4 FY26 PAT about 50% while EBITDA held?
How much of Oswego's $1.7B cash hit has insurance repaid, and when?
At 1.95x, which FY27 capex gets deferred if LME falls and leverage breaches 2x?

annual_report.business: India's largest integrated aluminium producer; world's largest flat-rolled aluminium producer and recycler via subsidiary Novelis; top-3 specialty alumina producer; India's leading copper smelter operator. Value chain spans bauxite mining, alumina refining, coal mining, power generation, smelting to downstream manufacturing across 48 units in 10 countries.

segments.name: Aluminium (India)
segments.comment: Fully integrated from mining to value-added products; target downstream 4x EBITDA growth

segments.name: Specialty Alumina
segments.comment: Among global top-3; scaling to ~1 MTPA capacity by FY2029-30

segments.name: Copper
segments.comment: Second-largest continuous cast rod producer outside China; expanding into alloys and recycling

segments.name: Novelis (Global Flat-Rolled Products)
segments.comment: World's largest FRP producer and aluminium recycler; 3x30 sustainability vision by 2030

annual_report.revenue_mix: Global footprint: North America, South America, Europe, Asia. Products: aluminium, copper metals; flat-rolled sheets; specialty alumina. End-markets: beverage packaging, automotive, aerospace, infrastructure.
strategy: Expand upstream capacity: 374KT Aditya smelter, 850KT Kansariguda alumina refinery expansion
Scale downstream premium products; target 4x EBITDA growth by FY2029-30
Novelis 3x30 vision: 75% recycled content, carbon footprint below 3MT per MT by 2030
Commission $5B Bay Minette facility (600KT FRP capacity) in FY2026-27
Achieve $350-400M structural cost savings at Novelis by FY2027-28
annual_report.outlook: Global aluminium demand ~1% growth to 75MT CY2026. India demand strong above GDP. Copper demand +2.7%. Long-term structural tailwinds from sustainability, EV adoption, lightweight material substitution.
annual_report.capex_plans: 374KT Aditya expansion, 850KT Kansariguda alumina refinery, $5B Bay Minette (600KT, FY2026-27), Novelis capacity expansions at Guthrie, UAL, Pindamonhangaba, Logan, Latchford.
risks: LME, forex, raw material volatility; upstream commodity price exposure
Rising imports from China and FTA countries; tariffs and geopolitical disruptions
Global supply chain disruptions; copper concentrate supply tightness
Scrap input competition and inflation; macroeconomic weakness in key markets
annual_report.flags: Oswego facility: two fires (Sept & Nov 2025) caused ~$1.7B negative cash flow, $100-150M EBITDA impact (pre-insurance recoveries). Plant insured subject to deductibles and policy limits. No auditor qualifications or related-party concerns noted.
